executive_summary: AUD/CHF trades at 0.58153 as of the 2026-09-03 close, meaning one Australian dollar buys 0.58153 Swiss francs, and the pair has risen 2.10% over one month, 3.45% over three months, 4.23% over six months and 10.75% over twelve — an unbroken grind that set a fresh fifty-two-week closing high of 0.58290 on 2026-09-02, one session before the payload spot date. The dominant bilateral narrative is the widest policy differential available in the developed world, +435bp between an RBA at 4.35% with a live conditional hiking bias and an SNB pinned at 0.00% on a conditional inflation forecast that assumes zero through 2028, harvested in a volatility regime with VIX at 14.51 and US high-yield spreads at 263bp; the franc has become the G10's funding currency of choice in place of the yen, and this cross is the purest destination of that rotation. What the bilateral lens adds to the two standalone dossiers is that they reinforce rather than cancel — the base dossier is tactically Bullish AUD and the quote dossier tactically Bearish CHF, which is the same trade counted through two doors — and that the same convergence appears in positioning, where speculators are long the base and short the quote simultaneously, so the pair's crowding is amplified rather than muted. Against that, the bilateral fundamentals point the other way with unusual coherence: a 13.5-point current-account differential (Australia −3.68% of GDP against Switzerland +9.77%), iron ore pinned at the floor of its annual range while gold — Switzerland's principal commodity correlate — is up 22.39% year-on-year, and a relative real exchange rate that leaves AUD roughly 14% expensive against CHF on BIS REER momentum. The direction verdict issued by the first pass is tactically Bullish at conviction 3 (net weighted score +0.2288) and strategically Neutral at conviction 2 (+0.0418), and the price payload broadly corroborates the tactical call: spot sits above a bullishly stacked 50/100/200-day complex and above a 200-week average it has just reclaimed, which is a stronger structural endorsement than the first pass could see without the chart. The caveat is arithmetic rather than rhetorical — Factors 1 and 3 alone supply 124% of the tactical net score, so this is a two-factor call on a rate gap and a volatility regime, and the September sequence is unhelpful because the SNB decides on 2026-09-24, five sessions before the RBA on 2026-09-29, so the quote leg reprices first.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no pair-level PPP series for AUD/CHF, so valuation is assessed on relative BIS real effective exchange rates, which both dossiers construct as a momentum proxy rather than a fair-value model. Australia's real broad effective rate stands at 115.92 for June 2026 after a +10.36-point twelve-month real appreciation — the largest in the eleven-currency benchmark set by more than double — while Switzerland's stands at 101.69, the 40th percentile of the cached 2024-01 to 2026-06 window and 1.03 points lower than a year earlier. The relative gap is therefore roughly +14.0%, the base dossier's own reading of AUD versus CHF and the mirror of the quote dossier's −11.39% reading of CHF versus AUD. That is the single largest real dislocation in the AUD complex outside the yen, and it is the valuation counterweight to everything the carry differential says. What the current level prices is a world in which the SNB stays at zero indefinitely while Australia holds the G10's highest rate, and both of those propositions are true today and fully in the price; a Bloomberg survey has economists who previously expected an SNB hike in 2026 now seeing no tightening before June 2027, with most expecting the first increase only in early 2028, which is precisely the assumption a 98th-percentile carry cross needs to remain valid. What the level does not price is the external-balance and commodity configuration set out in Factor 5, nor the 40th-percentile Swiss real rate, which removes the usual valuation objection to selling the franc and is the reason a mean-reversion case here is structural rather than tactical.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral policy differential is +435bp (RBA 4.35% against SNB 0.00%), and the ten-year differential is +452.1bp — the widest bilateral gap available in the G10+SGD set on both measures. On spot 0.58153 that carry is worth 253 pips a year, 21.1 pips a month, 126.5 pips over six months. Against an ATR(14) of 34 pips, a single average day's range erases roughly 1.6 months of accrued carry — the carry is real and among the best in the G10 but not large relative to the pair's own daily noise, so this is a directional position with a meaningful coupon rather than a coupon-harvesting position with incidental direction. Carry-to-volatility is the highest in the AUD complex on either denominator: 0.713 on 60-day realised vol of 6.10%, 0.675 on the gated 3M implied estimate of 6.446%, roughly 0.59 adjusting the implied estimate for its documented 14.4% understatement — still the best risk-adjusted carry available in the set. The carry regime is unambiguously working given VIX at 14.51 and high-yield OAS at 263bp; its break condition is volatility rather than rates, with realised volatility sustained above roughly 10% making 435bp uneconomic long before either central bank moves. The gated CME calendar-spread premium of −475.2bp annualised implies via covered interest parity a residual of roughly −40bp against the +435bp policy differential; the more parsimonious explanation is a measurement mismatch (Australian bank-bill rates running above the cash rate on priced tightening) rather than an adverse cross-currency basis, though both readings are recorded and the practical consequence is small either way.

For this pair the rate block is not one input among ten, it is the reason the pair exists as a trade.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is +435bp (RBA cash rate 4.35% against an SNB policy rate of 0.00%) and the 10-year differential is +452.1bp on the gated monthly series as of 2026-06-01 (AU 4.831% versus CH 0.31%). The level is old news and fully in the price; what matters tactically is the direction of change, and it is asymmetric to a degree unusual even for this pair. The RBA held unanimously on 11 August while explicitly reserving the right to raise the cash rate target further if upside risks materialise, and after the July CPI beat and a 1.1% month-on-month household spending surge the market prices roughly 47-50% for a hike to 4.60% at the 2026-09-29 decision and about 30bp cumulative by February 2027. Against that the SNB, which decides on 2026-09-24 with a quarterly assessment and a refreshed conditional inflation forecast, has essentially no upward pathway: headline CPI is 0.4% and core 0.3%, and its June forecast of 0.6%/0.6%/0.7% for 2026-2028 is conditioned on the rate staying at zero throughout. So the differential can widen to 460bp inside the tactical window and cannot mechanically narrow from the quote side. Transmission is the purest in the G10: with the highest bilateral carry available and no policy convergence risk, the cross is the mechanical destination of funding-currency-financed carry flow whenever volatility is contained.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential is the most durable single fact in this analysis and it is durable in an unusually literal sense: the SNB has published a forecast conditioned on zero through 2028, and the RBA has published forecasts showing trimmed-mean inflation above the 2-3% midpoint until early 2028. Neither central bank has a credible path to convergence inside the window. Every other AUD carry spread compresses over the horizon — 335bp to JPY narrows to 310bp on a consensus BoJ move, 185bp to NZD compresses toward 130bp, and the Fed is priced to add roughly twice the RBA's tightening — but the CHF spread has no such mechanism, which is precisely why the base dossier identifies AUD/CHF rather than AUD/USD as the cleanest strategic carry expression. The scheduled path is dated: RBA decisions on 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-08 carry the priced move to 4.60%, and the SNB assessment on 2026-12-10 is a quarterly projection round at which the only realistic surprises are a softening of the intervention stance or, in a small tail, a return toward negative rates that would widen the differential further. The strategic qualification is that the entire carry is already in the forward curve at a 40bp adverse basis, so the expected excess return from the differential alone is roughly zero to slightly negative; the direction it supports comes from the asymmetry of the reaction functions, not from the coupon.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is roughly 310bp (Australian headline 3.5% and trimmed mean 3.6% for July against Swiss headline 0.4% and core 0.3%) and it is the widest inflation gap in the developed world, but it is already the reason the policy differential is 435bp and is therefore captured in Factor 1 rather than adding independently here. The genuinely bilateral question is the surprise differential, and it currently runs the wrong way for the pair. Switzerland has been beating consensus by unusual margins — Q2 GDP at +1.5% quarter-on-quarter against a +0.2% to +0.4% range, the KOF barometer at 106.7 and its highest since November 2021 against a 103.0 forecast, industrial production at +5.5% year-on-year against a −4.7% forecast — while Australia's beats have been confined to prices with its activity data deteriorating on every measure that matters: unemployment at a post-COVID high of 4.5% with employment down 15,800, private capex −3.6% quarter-on-quarter against +0.8% consensus and construction work done −2.1%. The offsetting transmission asymmetry is real and it favours the pair: Australian price data changes the RBA reaction function and therefore the differential, whereas Swiss data of any quality changes nothing because the SNB is pinned. Netting a decisively pro-CHF surprise flow against a decisively pro-AUD transmission channel produces a genuine standoff, and Neutral is the honest reading rather than a default.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both growth stories deteriorate and the inflation differential narrows, which leaves the factor directionally empty. On the Australian side the RBA's own forecasts have trimmed mean falling to 3.3% by end-2026 while S&P projects real GDP slowing to 1.5% in fiscal 2027, business confidence sits at −19 and twenty-two points below its long-run average, and the base dossier assigns roughly a 40% probability to a per-capita recession. Swiss inflation is forecast at 0.6% on average and Australian inflation eases toward 3.3%, so the differential compresses from roughly 310bp toward 270bp — a marginal negative for the pair that does not survive rounding. With the weight reduced to 0.07 and both legs weakening, the factor contributes nothing directional and should not be forced into one.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Weights raised: the framework classifies AUD/CHF by name in its 'pure risk proxy pairs (high beta)' category, and this is the only factor in the set where the two legs are not merely different but structurally opposed — the highest-beta commodity currency in the G10 against the developed world's reference safe haven. For this pair risk appetite is a primary driver rather than a modifier, and understating it would misrepresent the pair's actual variance.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: AUD/CHF is the archetypal risk-proxy cross: the base is the most liquid G10 proxy for China and global cyclical demand, the quote is the reference haven, and the pair's beta to global risk appetite is therefore roughly the sum of two same-signed exposures rather than a partial offset. The current regime is unambiguously supportive. VIX closed at 14.51 on 2026-08-27, down 3.70 points from 18.21 a month earlier and in the lower quartile of its post-2020 distribution; US high-yield OAS is 263bp having tightened 21bp on the month and investment grade is 79bp, both near the tight end of their post-2022 ranges; and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed near cycle highs. Credit typically leads FX risk premia, and credit is signalling no stress at all. The transmission is direct and two-sided in the same direction: benign risk both bids the high-beta leg and removes the structural bid from the haven leg, which is why the CHF dossier scores its own risk factor franc-negative at 68 and the AUD dossier scores its risk factor AUD-positive at 60 — the rare case where two independently constructed dossiers reinforce rather than cancel. The identifiable contradiction, and it deserves flagging rather than glossing, is gold: at US$4,456.44 it is up 8.60% on the month and 22.39% on the year, so the franc's traditional haven correlate is being accumulated hard while the franc itself is sold. That is a correlation breakdown, not confirmation.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At one to six months the risk factor stops being a level signal and becomes a distribution, and for this pair specifically the distribution is the most left-skewed of any factor in the set. VIX at 14.51 and high-yield at 263bp are near the tight end of their post-2022 ranges: there is perhaps 20-40bp of further tightening available and unlimited widening. Both dossiers independently arrive at Neutral for this reason, and both then note the same fat tail from opposite sides — the base dossier documents AUD's violent risk-off convexity, and the quote dossier observes that the franc's payoff to a risk shock is convex and that its option surface is not charging for it. Three identifiable strategic vectors sit in the window: an unresolved Middle East conflict that already produced a round trip in Brent from US$100.31 on 2026-07-24 to US$88.24 on 2026-08-25; a synchronised developed-market tightening cycle running into slowing growth, historically associated with credit events at a two-to-four-quarter lag; and China in manufacturing contraction at a PMI of 49.8 with only a targeted CNY800bn financing facility rather than broad reflation. Offsetting these, AI-related investment is genuinely supporting trading-partner growth on the RBA's own assessment. The honest verdict is that the expected value is close to zero while the variance is large and one-sided, which is Neutral with a fat left tail rather than an absence of view.

Confidence falls from 68 to 55 to reflect that risk-regime forecasting at six months has very little skill.

Against that, being short this cross costs 435bp per annum, roughly 21 pips per month, and the base leg's structural asset-manager short has been wrong through a full year of appreciation — so positioning strategically functions as an amplifier of whichever fundamental outcome arrives rather than as an independent directional signal, which is why confidence is 52.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Strategic weight raised: this is the widest external-balance gap available in the G10 — a record Australian current-account deficit of −3.68% of GDP against a Swiss surplus of +9.77%, a 13.5-point differential, with a Swiss net international investment position of roughly 120% of GDP on one side and a commodity export base facing structural supply increases on the other. Both parent dossiers score this factor in the same direction for the pair, which makes it the most reinforcing bilateral input in the set and the one that most deserves additional strategic weight.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external differential is enormous and is currently moving against the pair on both legs at once. Switzerland, over the same window, posted a July trade surplus of CHF 8.1bn, the largest since the series began in January 1950, on exports up 13.8% and imports down 4.5%, against a current account of 9.77% of GDP. Direct bilateral trade is immaterial to the cross: on IMF DOTS 2024 data Australia exported USD 1.4bn of goods to Switzerland and imported USD 3.0bn, a net Australian deficit of USD 1.6bn, a rounding error against either economy's total flows — so transmission runs entirely through third-party commodity and financial channels. Those channels currently point the same way. Iron ore, roughly 35% of Australian export revenue, sits at US$95.34 against a fifty-two-week range of US$93.66-111.42 — at the floor — while gold at US$4,456.44 is up 8.60% on the month and is the franc's principal commodity correlate given Switzerland's position as the world's largest refining hub. The one genuine offset is energy: Newcastle coal near US$130/t and Japanese LNG at US$19.0/mmbtu are lifting Australian export receipts now, while Brent's fall from US$100.31 to US$88.24 is a terms-of-trade gain for a Switzerland that imports all of its fossil energy.

Applying the framework's direction rules channel by channel and netting for AUD/CHF: iron ore up gives ++AUD and is broadly neutral-to-mildly-negative for an importer, so iron ore up is pair-positive — and iron ore is at its annual floor with structural supply arriving, so the current state of this channel is pair-negative. Gold up gives +CHF, and gold is up 22.39% year-on-year, so this channel is currently pair-negative. Oil up gives +AUD mildly through the coal/LNG substitution complex and the RBA's own oil-to-inflation-to-policy chain, and is negative for an all-import energy consumer, so on the narrow terms-of-trade channel oil up is pair-positive — but in the 2026 regime an oil spike arrives via Middle East escalation, a risk-off event, and for a pure risk-proxy cross the haven channel dominates the terms-of-trade channel. Netting all three: the two dominant commodity channels, iron ore and gold, are both currently pair-negative, and the oil channel is pair-negative in both directions once risk transmission is included. Net commodity exposure of AUD/CHF is unambiguously negative in the current configuration, and this is the mechanical basis for the strategic Bearish stance at a 0.19 weight.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The guidance divergence on this pair is the widest available anywhere in the G10 and it is one-sided in the same direction on both legs. The RBA held unanimously on 11 August with an explicit conditional hiking sentence — it will do what it considers necessary including increasing the cash rate target further if upside risks materialise — and the 25 August minutes went further, disclosing that the Board actively debated tightening pre-emptively and naming the monthly inflation, employment and housing reports as the evidence that would settle the question before the 2026-09-29 decision. A unanimous hold with a conditional hike sentence removes the dovish-dissent discount the market normally applies. The SNB, meanwhile, has given the market something rarer than guidance: an explicitly asymmetric statement of its exchange-rate reaction function, telling the market on 18 June that it has an increased willingness to intervene to counter a rapid and excessive appreciation of the franc, with no corresponding commitment against depreciation, reaffirmed by Chairman Schlegel on 8 July. For AUD/CHF that combination is a base-currency central bank threatening to raise its rate and a quote-currency central bank promising to sell its own currency if it rallies. Sequence matters and it is unfavourable rather than favourable: the SNB assessment on 2026-09-24 carries a projection round and lands five sessions before the RBA on 2026-09-29, so the quote leg reprices first and a softening of the intervention language — assessed at roughly 25% — would hit the cross before the base leg gets its turn.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically the factor carries 0.12 and it is the most durable of the pair-supportive inputs because it is a statement about reaction functions rather than about data. The RBA has published forecasts showing inflation above the midpoint until early 2028 and has framed itself as focused on ensuring high inflation does not become embedded, which anchors the front end of the Australian curve and by extension the carry; a central bank with that framing does not begin easing inside six months. The SNB's structural incentive over the same window is reinforced rather than weakened: Switzerland's exports face Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs of up to 15%, which raises its sensitivity to any further competitiveness loss through the exchange rate, and Schlegel has repeatedly cited the undesirable side effects of negative rates, so intervention rather than sub-zero policy is the stated active lever, backed by roughly CHF 889.6bn of official reserve assets. Both credibility records are strong, with two qualifications that cut in opposite directions. The RBA's hawkish bias is explicitly conditional on an oil supply shock it does not control, and Brent has already fallen 12.0% in a month — if that continues the guidance premium in the base leg fades faster than priced. The SNB's guidance is written to counter appreciation, so it offers no support to a short-franc position if the pair simply drifts, and a bank that surprised the market by 30% in January 2015 caps how far any SNB commitment can be trusted. The next high-signal events are the RBA on 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-08 and the SNB quarterly assessment on 2026-12-10.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The event distribution for this specific cross is skewed against it, because the events capable of moving a pure risk-proxy pair by 2% or more in four weeks are overwhelmingly risk-off events, and risk-off is negative on both legs simultaneously. The dominant undated variable is the Middle East conflict, and the two economies sit on opposite sides of it in the way that matters least and the same side in the way that matters most: Australia gains export receipts and a hawkish RBA from an oil supply disruption while Switzerland loses on its import bill, but a conflict-driven risk shock bids the franc as the reference haven and sells the highest-beta G10 currency, and the haven channel dominates for this cross. Bilateral political risk between the two economies is negligible — there is no trade dispute, no sanctions exposure and, on IMF DOTS 2024 data, only USD 4.4bn of two-way goods trade. The dated Swiss-specific item is the 27 September federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality, which would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions absent a UN mandate; August polling has 62% against and 36% in favour, so rejection is the base case and the modal outcome is a non-event, with roughly a 20% passage tail whose franc implications are genuinely two-sided. The clustering is unusual: the SNB assessment on 2026-09-24, the referendum on 2026-09-27 and the RBA on 2026-09-29 fall inside six days, and on the pair's own gated vol surface no event premium whatsoever is being charged for any of it.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.0418 sits inside the −0.10 to +0.10 band, so the derived stance is Neutral and is applied mechanically. The structure behind the number matters far more than the number. This is not ten indifferent factors: it is two large, well-identified and directly opposed blocs that very nearly cancel. On the positive side, Policy and Rates contributes +0.1674 at a 0.27 weight and Guidance contributes +0.0840 at 0.12, a combined +0.2514 that amounts to a single proposition — a 435bp differential with no compression pathway, held in place by a central bank that has promised to sell its own currency if it rallies. On the negative side, External Balance contributes −0.1330 at its raised 0.19 weight, with Positioning at −0.0312, Event Risk at −0.0280 and Market Structure at −0.0174, a combined −0.2096 that amounts to a second single proposition — a 13.5-point current-account differential, a commodity complex running the wrong way on both legs, and a crowded carry position in a pair near a twelve-month extreme. Four factors score zero and in each case the zero is a genuine two-sided assessment. Mapping to conviction: +0.0418 with genuine two-sided offsets and no dominant factor maps to conviction 2 of 5 — a deliberate Neutral held with low conviction because the offsetting forces are individually large and could resolve either way. Conviction 2 rather than 1 is justified because the neutrality is a balance of two identified forces each worth roughly 0.25 of weighted score, which makes the composition actionable even though the direction is not.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the pair becomes a direct contest between the widest carry differential in the G10 and the widest external-balance differential in the G10, and they very nearly cancel. Policy and Rates at 0.27 and Guidance at 0.12 carry the positive case: 435bp with no compression pathway, an RBA whose own published forecasts keep inflation above the midpoint until early 2028 and which decides on 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-08, and an SNB whose conditional forecast is pinned at 0.00% through 2028 and whose stated reaction function is explicitly asymmetric against franc strength, reaffirmed by Schlegel and backed by roughly CHF 889.6bn of reserves — a reading that recent survey evidence strengthens, since economists who had expected an SNB hike in 2026 now see no tightening before June 2027 and most expect the first increase only in early 2028. External Balance at its raised 0.19 weight carries the negative case, and it is the deepest single bilateral fact in the analysis: a record Australian current-account deficit of A$27.1bn at −3.68% of GDP with a consensus of A$−29.7bn for Q2 and terms of trade already down 4.4% quarter-on-quarter, against a Swiss surplus of 9.77% of GDP, a net international investment position of CHF 974bn worth roughly 120% of annual output, and the largest monthly trade surplus since the series began in 1950. The two dossiers interact destructively rather than constructively at this horizon, and that is the honest reading: the same high rates that make Factor 1 positive are what produce the Australian growth deterioration that turns Factor 2 neutral, and the same oil shock that keeps the RBA hawkish in Factor 6 is what widens the Australian import bill in Factor 5. Bilateral-specific modifications to the standalone views are three. First, direct trade is immaterial — USD 4.4bn of two-way goods flow on IMF DOTS 2024 data, essentially gold for pharmaceuticals — so the cross trades third-party channels, and both dominant ones run against it: iron ore at roughly 35% of Australian export revenue sits at US$95.34 with 2026 consensus at US$94-96 and approximately 20Mt of Simandou supply arriving, while gold, the franc's principal correlate given Swiss refining, is up 22.39% on the year. Second, oil is adverse in both directions, because an escalation-driven spike delivers a haven bid and a growth hit that swamp the terms-of-trade gain, while a resolution deflates the coal and LNG windfall and the RBA's own stated oil-to-inflation-to-policy chain at once. Third, the pair is where the franc's multi-decade structural uptrend has genuinely broken, and the price payload confirms it precisely: weeksSinceCloseAbove200w is zero, spot is 1.88% above a 200-week average of 0.57080, and that average is declining at 0.000446 per week, so the reclaim gets structurally easier to hold with time rather than harder. On what is priced against what we expect, the forward curve discounts 475.2bp annualised — roughly 40bp more than the policy differential — so the market has priced the coupon in full and requires spot to hold for the position to earn it; we agree there is no carry edge and disagree only with the six-month vol estimate of 6.701%, which prices a one-standard-deviation move of about 4.7% for a pair with documented 30%-class tails on both legs. Path of least resistance is sideways with episodic downside: the carry keeps the pair supported while nothing goes wrong, and the negative catalysts — Australian Q3 CPI in late October, the RBA on 2026-11-03, the SNB projection round on 2026-12-10, iron ore supply and the 31 December funding turn — are scheduled. Conviction is 2 because the two dominant blocs are individually large and genuinely opposed, and because the tie is broken by two variables nobody can forecast at six months: whether the Middle East oil shock persists, and whether Chinese steel output stabilises.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Among AUD crosses AUD/CHF ranks mid-pack strategically rather than first: the carry is the best available and the most durable, but pairing the G10's worst external position with its best produces a 13.5-point current-account gap that no other AUD cross carries, so it ranks behind AUD/NZD as a convergence expression and behind AUD/JPY on external symmetry, while ranking ahead of AUD/USD on carry durability. Among CHF crosses it ranks first on carry and last on external balance simultaneously, which is the clearest single statement of why the strategic verdict is Neutral. Across the whole G10 set it is the highest-conviction carry pair and the lowest-conviction fundamental pair, and those two facts are not reconcilable at a six-month horizon.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic shape is a high-level range that erodes, closest to a rounded top than to a trend, and it is policy-dated. Phase one, September through late October, is the pair's strongest window: the differential is at its widest, the RBA repricing is live, the carry regime is intact and the fresh 200-week reclaim gives trend-following capital a reason to stay long — expect the pair to work between roughly 0.5775 and 0.5915, testing the five-touch 0.58879-0.59150 band at least once. The inflection is the Australian Q3 CPI in the last week of October and the RBA decision on 2026-11-03, which together resolve whether the July inflation acceleration was signal or noise; that is also the moment the base leg runs out of policy news for a quarter. Phase two, November into February, is where the terms-of-trade decay and the balance-of-payments arithmetic become visible without a countervailing rate story, and where the 31 December dollar-funding turn mechanically forces a reduction of exactly this position — expect a drift back toward 0.5705-0.5745, the four-touch/200-week confluence, with the six-touch 0.56309-0.56720 band as the floor that defines whether the six-month carry has been kept or given back. Volatility should rise through the December policy cluster, when the RBA on 2026-12-08 and the SNB on 2026-12-10 land inside three days into thin liquidity, and the 6.701% six-month implied estimate is likely to be exceeded by realised volatility in that window. The dominant risk to this path is that it is too orderly: a pure risk-proxy cross at the 98th percentile of its range, with both legs' speculative positioning on the same side and no skew observable at all, does not usually mean-revert gently.

risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: A Neutral spot view on this pair is not a neutral total-return view. The expected value of the direction is −0.30%; the expected value of the position is +1.87%, because the coupon is large enough to dominate a flat-to-negative spot expectation and to absorb more than half of a −4.56% adverse scenario. The label 'Neutral' is correct as a statement about which way the pair goes and understates the case for owning it: the strategic verdict is a direction call, not an allocation call, and the allocation implied by the same numbers is a modest long held for the coupon with the invalidators treated as hard rather than advisory, because the negative skew is real and 4.56% of adverse spot is 2.1 years of carry.

consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Neutral at AUD/CHF 0.5820 at the six-month mark, with a positive total-return expectation of +1.87% including carry
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: roughly 1% to 4% above the derived cross consensus of 0.562 to 0.577
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: There is no bank research forecast for AUD/CHF as a cross. The defensible reference point is a derived cross built from the two legs' published bank forecasts: AUD/USD clusters at 0.71-0.73 and USD/CHF clusters at 0.78-0.79, giving a derived cross of roughly 0.562-0.577, or 1% to 3.5% below the payload spot of 0.58153. We differ for three specific reasons. First, the September FOMC is genuinely two-sided at 60.4% priced for a hike, which removes the load-bearing assumption of the franc-bullish dollar leg embedded in the derived consensus. Second, we weigh the external-balance differential at 0.19 strategically — a 13.5-point current-account gap with iron ore at its annual floor and gold up 22.39% — which no single-currency forecast captures because it only exists bilaterally. Third, we weigh the SNB's asymmetric guidance at 0.12, and that guidance is written to counter appreciation only, which truncates the right tail of exactly the franc rally the consensus dollar leg requires. The divergence is one of internal consistency rather than of magnitude: the derived consensus is simultaneously long the franc against the dollar on Fed-easing expectations and constructive on AUD against the dollar on RBA repricing, a combination that only produces a lower AUD/CHF in a narrow set of circumstances.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Roughly 100 to 200 pips of advantage over the derived cluster, but more usefully the recognition that the tradeable content of this pair sits inside the next four to eight weeks and is anchored to two dated decisions, after which the forward curve — which embeds nothing but the differential — is very nearly the right forecast.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the derived consensus is right and the franc firms on Fed easing while Chinese steel demand deteriorates, the negative bloc dominates, the strategic Neutral proves to have been a Bearish call held one notch too politely, and 435bp of carry is the only thing standing between a −4.6% spot move and a −2.4% total return. If instead the RBA delivers and the SNB softens nothing, the tactical Bullish extends well past four weeks, both legs' crowded positioning amplifies rather than caps the move, and a strategic Neutral leaves the G10's best carry pair unowned through the part of the cycle when carry works.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons are not aligned: tactically Bullish at conviction 3 with a net weighted score of +0.2288, strategically Neutral at conviction 2 with +0.0418, a divergence of 0.1870. The divergence is almost entirely mechanical rather than a change of view. Two reweightings do most of it: External Balance moves from 0.06 tactically to 0.19 strategically while holding a Bearish stance and rising in confidence from 58 to 70, which alone shifts the score by −0.0982, and Risk Appetite flips from Bullish 68 at a 0.14 weight to Neutral at 0.08, removing a further −0.0952. Against those, USD Liquidity gives up its +0.0420 tactical contribution to a strategic Neutral, and Inflation & Growth is Neutral at both horizons and contributes nothing either way. The economic content is straightforward: over two to four weeks the pair trades the reaction functions of two central banks, one of which has a scheduled and half-priced chance to widen the differential and the other of which cannot narrow it; over one to six months it trades the balance of payments and the commodity complex, and both of those are deteriorating for the base leg while the quote leg runs a near-10%-of-GDP surplus.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Late October to mid-November 2026, specifically the Australian Q3 CPI in the last week of October and the RBA decision on 2026-11-03. Once the RBA has either delivered 4.60% or credibly deferred, there is no further base-leg policy news for at least a quarter and the differential stops being a variable; attention then rotates to the Australian Q3 current account and terms of trade, the arrival of Simandou supply, and the SNB projection round on 2026-12-10.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the tactical Bullish as a defined-horizon view that terminates at or before the 2026-11-03 RBA decision, and do not roll it into the strategic window without re-underwriting External Balance at its 0.19 weight. The strategic Neutral is not a reason to be flat, for the total-return reason set out above, but it is a reason to stop expressing this pair as a directional view and to hold it as a coupon position with hard invalidation at the 200-week average. The sequence within the tactical window is unfavourable: the SNB assessment on 2026-09-24 precedes the RBA on 2026-09-29, so the single most likely adverse surprise for the pair lands before the base leg's own catalyst, and the pair's vol surface is charging nothing for either.

catalysts.event: Australia Q2 Balance of Payments and current account
catalysts.rationale: Consensus is A$−29.7bn against a record A$−27.1bn in Q1, which would be a second consecutive record deficit at above 4% of GDP. The current account is the observable expression of Factor 5, which carries a raised 0.19 strategic weight for this pair specifically because the quote economy runs a 9.77%-of-GDP surplus against it — a 13.5-point differential. A print worse than A$−30bn widens the widest external gap in the G10 and lands on the base leg alone.

Consensus is +0.3% quarter-on-quarter but the partials were uniformly weak — capex −3.6% against +0.8%, construction work done −2.1% against +0.5%, plant and machinery capex −8.9%. A sub-0.2% print materially reduces the roughly 47-50% priced for the 2026-09-29 RBA decision, and since 84% of this pair's positive tactical contribution comes from the rate and guidance complex, base-leg growth disappointment transmits to the cross with no quote-leg offset available.

catalysts.event: Switzerland detailed Q2 GDP and August CPI, plus Australia July trade balance
catalysts.rationale: A rare same-day double on both legs. Swiss Q2 detail follows a +1.5% flash against a +0.2-0.4% consensus with risk skewed higher after the +5.5% industrial production beat, while August CPI at a 0.0% month-on-month consensus is more likely to undershoot with Brent 12 dollars off its high. Swiss strength without inflation is franc-ambiguous because the SNB is pinned at zero regardless; the Australian July trade release is the first published read on whether the coal and LNG windfall converted into receipts.

catalysts.event: CFTC Commitments of Traders for both legs
catalysts.rationale: The only release that speaks to both legs of the crowding problem at once. Base-leg leveraged funds at +54,061 contracts and 18.2% of open interest on the cached tranche would enter the historical reversal zone above 65,000, while the franc aggregate at −19.9k has room to rebuild toward the notable threshold at −30,000. A simultaneous base-leg build and franc-short rebuild confirms trend participation in the cross; base-leg liquidation with continued franc covering is the two-leg unwind Factor 4 identifies.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: No dollar leg exists in this cross, so the transmission is through the dollar smile. A hike, priced at 60.4% after the 2026-08-28 Jackson Hole keynote, moves the dollar toward the exceptionalism end where the base currency structurally underperforms and away from the benign middle that is currently the franc's worst environment — negative for the pair. A hold weakens the dollar further from 118.06 on the broad index and deepens the rotation into high beta out of funding currencies, which is positive.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank monetary policy assessment (quarterly, refreshed conditional inflation forecast)
catalysts.rationale: A hold at 0.00% is effectively certain, so the entire content is the language and the refreshed forecast. Retention of the increased willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation sustains the asymmetric cap that carries 0.12 of the strategic weight in Factor 6. The material risk to the pair is removal or softening of that sentence, assessed at roughly 25%, which would read as tolerance of a stronger franc — and it lands five sessions before the base leg gets its own catalyst.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality
catalysts.rationale: Passage would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions against belligerent states absent a UN Security Council mandate and constrain NATO cooperation, forcing re-examination of the framework under which roughly CHF 8.5bn of Russian-linked assets are frozen. August polling has 62% against and 36% in favour, so rejection is the strong base case and the modal outcome is a non-event; the roughly 20% passage tail is genuinely two-sided for the franc's haven premium and is being carried for free given the contango in the pair's vol surface.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
catalysts.rationale: The single largest binary for this pair inside the tactical window. Roughly 47-50% is priced for a move to 4.60%, which would take the bilateral differential from 435bp to 460bp against a quote leg that decided five sessions earlier and cannot move in the franc's favour. The statement language matters as much as the decision: removal of the conditional hiking sentence would be a major dovish surprise into a market priced for the opposite, and would strip the pair of the factor supplying 84% of its positive tactical contribution.

Australia publishes headline and trimmed-mean CPI quarterly rather than monthly, compressing three months of expectations into one number and producing outsized reactions. This is the release that resolves the central market disagreement — whether the July acceleration was signal, as NAB, CBA, ANZ and Goldman argue, or noise, as Westpac maintains. Because the quote leg's inflation is 0.4% and structurally incapable of surprising into a policy change, this print is effectively the pair's only remaining inflation catalyst and is the identified tactical-to-strategic inflection.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
catalysts.rationale: CBA, ANZ, Goldman Sachs and UBS all locate the move to 4.60% here rather than in September, so this is where the differential most likely reaches 460bp. It is also the handover point between horizons: once the RBA has delivered or credibly deferred, there is no base-leg policy news for a quarter and the pair's attention rotates to the balance of payments.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
catalysts.rationale: A move to 4.60% by December is fully priced, which makes the configuration asymmetric: delivery is neutral for the pair and non-delivery is sharply negative, collapsing roughly 30bp of priced tightening on the only leg capable of moving. It falls two days before the quote leg's own projection round, so the pair faces both central banks inside three days into year-end illiquidity, and neither event can widen the differential beyond what is already in the curve.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank monetary policy assessment (quarterly, refreshed conditional inflation forecast)
catalysts.rationale: The final quote-leg decision of 2026 and the point at which the SNB will have four more months of data on whether its June average forecast of 0.6% for 2026 held. The rate is all but certain to remain at 0.00%, so the variables are the intervention language and any revision to the 2027-2028 forecast path. A revision toward zero inflation would reopen the negative-rate tail, widening the differential and being pair-positive; abandonment of the intervention stance would be pair-negative.

The 31 December turn is the largest recurring dollar-funding squeeze in the calendar and the most reliable seasonal source of cross-currency basis widening. Because AUD/CHF is the purest carry expression in the G10 — 435bp funded in the zero-rate leg — a basis widening mechanically forces a reduction of exactly this position, and the pair already prices roughly 40bp above the policy differential in its forward curve before any seasonal widening. With the three-month EUR/USD basis last observed at only −16 to −20bp there is unusual room for it to widen.

assumptions: Price payload provenance: derived analytics deliver 130 weekday bars over 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, spot 0.58153 at spotDate 2026-09-03; moving averages, zones, 52-week statistics and 200-week figures are computed over the full stored history 2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03 (4,879 weekday bars), not the 130 bars shown.

Spot date (2026-09-03) is two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date at which both dossiers and the direction verdict are struck; the gap is disclosed rather than resolved, and all levels/targets/pips are anchored to payload spot.

Percentile discrepancy: both parent dossiers record the 100th percentile of the 52-week range; the payload's own computation gives 98th on both range and close bases. The payload governs for price-derived metrics; the settled Factor 9 stance, resting partly on the 100th-percentile reading, stands as issued.

Implied volatility is a triangulated estimate, not a quote: AUD/CHF has no listed option; the store's method feeds a realised correlation of 0.611 in place of an unobservable implied one, and documents understating direct quotes by a median 14.4% across seventeen pairs — the three tenors quoted are treated as floors.

Risk reversals are unobservable for this cross; no 25-delta skew exists for AUD/CHF and neither dossier could source one for the franc leg, so skew discussion rests on the base leg's own surface and documented franc skew behaviour around SNB communication — a genuine analytical gap.

Funding block residual: the gated CME calendar-spread premium of −475.2bp annualised implies via covered interest parity a roughly −40bp residual against the +435bp policy differential; the more parsimonious explanation is a money-market rate mismatch (Australian bank-bill rates above cash rate on priced tightening) rather than an adverse basis — both readings are recorded and neither changes the settled stance.

Rate block dates differ: AUD policy rate as of 2026-07-01, CHF as of 2026-09-01; confirmed the AU rate was held unanimously on 2026-08-11 so the cached level is treated as live; the 10-year differential is computed from monthly series as of 2026-06-01 and never presented as a live level.

Direction verdict is carried, not re-derived: all ten factor stances, confidences, evidence_type labels, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, rankings, cross-horizon analysis, consensus divergence and catalysts are reproduced verbatim from the first pass; net_stance is derived mechanically from net_weighted_score at both horizons.
Factor 9 is the only pair_price_action factor; every other factor stance rests on non-price evidence and declares it.
Weight adjustments: six factors adjusted (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 10), each within the ±0.05 limit and both horizons summing to exactly 1.00, each justified against a specific bilateral condition.

Bilateral trade data (IMF DOTS 2024) is taken verbatim and not re-estimated; the two reporting directions disagree (Australia reports USD 1.4bn exports to Switzerland; Switzerland reports USD 4.6bn imports from Australia), a discrepancy consistent with gold/precious-metals routing through Swiss refining; the conclusion that the bilateral goods channel is immaterial holds on either reporting basis.

No bank forecast exists for this cross; bank_consensus_forecast is null. The derived cross built from the two legs' published USD forecasts is labelled a derivation throughout; retail extrapolation and algorithmic-model sites are reported as such and not treated as consensus.

Inherited flags from the parent dossiers' own adversarial verification are reproduced where used: Australian net debt of 19.9% of GDP is not carried by the cited PBO snapshot (which shows gross debt peaking at 35.8%); the Swiss debt ratio varies 30-41% across measurement bases; SNB total official reserve assets of CHF 889.6bn rests on an unmatched calendar entry; the three-month EUR/USD basis of −16 to −20bp is roughly 110 days stale; the Swiss July trade surplus is corroborated in a CHF 8.1-8.4bn range; both legs' 10-year yields are 92 days old at the valuation date.

Interpretive choices made without a user present: (a) payload's 98th-percentile reading supersedes the dossiers' 100th for narrative while the settled Factor 9 stance is untouched; (b) the residual 40bp in the funding block is presented with both sign interpretations; (c) scenario and invalidator probabilities are analyst judgements calibrated to the factor analysis, not options-implied, because no distribution exists for a cross with no listed option; (d) the tactical stop is placed at the 200-week/four-touch confluence rather than a round number; (e) the strategic total-return observation is presented as an addendum to Risk/Reward rather than a challenge to the Neutral stance.
